title: The Record With No First Page: a Licenciada in Choreographic Composition, and a Second Name on the Pole
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: A Record With No First Page

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the record that begins in the middle
stops.date_confidence: earliest date attested anywhere in her own documents; no birth date, birthplace, cohort year or graduation year is recorded in any reachable source, an absence verified on the two likeliest ones rather than merely unsearched
stops.campa: Every reachable account of her begins in the middle. Her university profile gives a degree and a method and no birth date. Her portfolio gives a working life and no first page. Both were read to the end. Neither carries a birthplace, a school before the university, a year of entry or a year of graduation, and no other reachable source carries them either. A dancer's origin is normally the first thing a programme prints. The earliest date she sets down herself is 2019. By then she is already co-directing.
sources: UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile, movimiento.una.edu.ar/graduadxs/massacesi-emilia_26 (gap confirmed on the page itself)
Massacesi portfolio PDF, 14 pp., read in full
suggested_refs: The UNA graduate roll of the Departamento de Artes del Movimiento, which prints her degree and no dates

stops.name: Martín Rodríguez 444, the licenciatura
stops.date_confidence: placed at the earliest attested year of her working life; the degree itself carries no year on the graduate roll
stops.campa: The Universidad Nacional de las Artes grants her the Licenciatura en Composición Coreográfica, mención Danza. Its Departamento de Artes del Movimiento keeps a graduate roll, and the roll prints her name, her degree and her working biography with no year attached to any of it: not entry, not completion. She is a licenciada of a school whose published record does not say when she was in it. Where the school itself stands is not in doubt. It is at Martín Rodríguez 444, a few blocks off the Riachuelo in La Boca.
stops.quote: Creadora, bailarina, directora escénica y docente. Licenciada en Composición Coreográfica mención Danza.
stops.quote_source: UNA Departamento de Artes del Movimiento, graduate profile (author-supplied bio line), fetched 2026-08-16
sources: UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile, movimiento.una.edu.ar/graduadxs/massacesi-emilia_26
suggested_refs: The UNA Artes del Movimiento building, Martín Rodríguez 444, La Boca

stops.name: La Boca, the archive crossed with popular languages
stops.date_confidence: undated statement on a current institutional page; placed with the licenciatura
stops.campa: The same page states her method in one sentence: her work consists of denaturalizing the habits of composition and creation in academic scenic dance, through the historical reconstruction of a local archive and its crossing with popular languages. It is the only statement of purpose she has published anywhere, and everything that follows can be read against it, the theatre work and the pole competitions alike. The archive is not named. The popular languages are not listed. Which local archive does a licenciada in choreographic composition reconstruct, and against what?
stops.quote: Su trabajo artístico consiste en desnaturalizar los hábitos de composición y creación en danza académica escénica a través de la reconstrucción histórica de un archivo local y el cruce con lenguajes populares.
stops.quote_source: UNA Departamento de Artes del Movimiento, graduate profile (author-supplied method statement), fetched 2026-08-16
sources: UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile, movimiento.una.edu.ar/graduadxs/massacesi-emilia_26
suggested_refs: The unnamed local dance archive that her method statement reconstructs

stops.name: El Taller de Omar, two solos shown together
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio; the venue has no findable address, so the pin is the city-level Buenos Aires anchor rather than a street
stops.campa: In a room called El Taller de Omar she and Lucila Schmidt open Solos Compartidos: two solos shown together, Café Mandolina and Pigmenta, co-directed and danced by the two of them. Her university's graduate page confirms Schmidt's co-direction; the portfolio supplies the years. The venue has no findable address. It appears in her portfolio as a name and nowhere else reachable, so the pin falls on the city rather than the street. The run will hold three years.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.9
UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile (confirms Schmidt co-direction)
suggested_refs: El Taller de Omar, Buenos Aires, address unrecorded in any reachable source

stops.name: El Taller de Omar, the run closes
stops.date_confidence: closing year attested in the portfolio; no month or performance count anywhere
stops.campa: Solos Compartidos runs from 2019 to 2021 and then stops. No programme, no press notice, no recording, no audience count survives. Her university's page records that Prodanza, the city dance fund, supported two of her works, without saying which two. What was shown in that room across three seasons is recoverable now as a title and a pair of names, Massacesi and Schmidt, each directing the other. The portfolio prints two photographs and the years beneath them.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.9
UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile (Prodanza support, works unnamed)
suggested_refs: Prodanza, the Buenos Aires city dance fund, whose two grants to her are unnamed

stops.name: El Taller de Omar, a dew called Automovilina
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio; venue unlocated, city-level pin
stops.campa: In the same room she makes a piece alone: Un rocío llamado Automovilina, credited directora e intérprete, with no co-author beside her. It is the first work in the record that is entirely hers, and the last of the Taller de Omar entries. Nothing else about it was set down anywhere a reader outside that room can reach. What survives is a photograph on page seven of a document she built herself, and a title that names a dew and a fuel. The year is 2021.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.7
suggested_refs: Un rocío llamado Automovilina, 2021, surviving as one portfolio photograph

stops.name: Paseo La Plaza, the New Face silver
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio only; no competition results page was reachable in any pass
stops.campa: On Avenida Corrientes, in the Paseo La Plaza, a competitor enters the New Face category of Exotic Generation Argentina under the name Emilia Portman. The routine is called Medusa. Natah Szuka photographs it. She takes silver, and the championship publishes no results a reader outside can reach, so the placing stands on her own document. From here the second name carries the pole work and Massacesi carries the theatre. It is the first competition in the record, and the first appearance of the second name.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.14, photo credit Natah Szuka
suggested_refs: Exotic Generation Argentina 2021, New Face category; no results page reachable

stops.name: Teatro Libre, Bogotá, the fox spirit
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio; the portfolio names only Teatro Libre, Bogotá, and Teatro Libre runs two houses, so which one is unstated
stops.campa: She leaves the country for the first time in the record, to Bogotá, for Exotic Generation Latinoamérica at the Teatro Libre. Pole Maniax photographs it. Her portfolio names the theatre and the city and no more, and Teatro Libre runs two houses. In the Flow category she takes silver and the prize for best choreography with a routine called Kitsune Kitten Fantasy: a fox spirit borrowed from Japan, danced on a pole in Colombia by an Argentine licenciada in choreographic composition.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.11, photo credit Pole Maniax
suggested_refs: Teatro Libre, Bogotá, which runs two houses, de Chapinero and del Centro

stops.name: Teatro del Globo, the Naruto routine
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio only; the Pole-up tournament's own results were unreachable
stops.campa: At the Teatro del Globo on Marcelo T. de Alvear she competes in the Pole-up tournament, High Heels Pro category, with a routine adapted from the anime Naruto, and takes bronze. Romina Soledad photographs it. The tournament publishes no results page reachable from outside, so the bronze, like the silver before it, rests on her portfolio. The crossing with popular languages that her method statement promises is here entirely literal: a manga serial, a stripper heel, a proscenium house and a jury, in one room, on one afternoon.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.12, photo credit Romina Soledad
suggested_refs: Teatro del Globo, Marcelo T. de Alvear 1155, Buenos Aires

stops.name: The Roxy Live!, Salvaje takes the Dance Expert
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio; the venue string Teatro The Roxy resolves to The Roxy Live!, Av. Coronel Niceto Vega 5542, Palermo, geocoded by OpenStreetMap
stops.campa: Her portfolio calls the venue Teatro The Roxy. The house is The Roxy Live! on Avenida Coronel Niceto Vega in Palermo, a rock club rather than a theatre. In the Dance Expert category of the Hypnotic Experience Show she dances a routine called Salvaje. She takes first place, the only first place in the record; the three placings before it are two silvers and a bronze. The portfolio is saved for the last time in June of the same year and records no competition after this one.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.10, photo credit Natah Szuka

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the nightclubs named without naming
stops.date_confidence: undated institutional statement; placed at the last competition year the portfolio records
stops.campa: Her university states, in the last paragraph of her graduate biography, that alongside the academic work she investigates non-academic scenic fields such as exotic pole dance, developing professionally as a dancer and performer in nightclubs and as an athlete in high-performance competition, prizewinning nationally and internationally, under the pseudonym Emilia Portman / Em Port. A national university prints the pseudonym in its own graduate roll, in the same paragraph as the nightclubs. It names no club and gives no date.
stops.quote: Paralelamente investiga otros campos escénicos no académicos como el exotic pole dance, desarrollándose profesionalmente como bailarina y performer en clubes nocturnos y como atleta en competiciones de alto rendimiento, habiendo sido premiada en distintos campeonatos nacionales e internacionales, bajo el pseudónimo Emilia Portman / Em Port.
stops.quote_source: UNA Departamento de Artes del Movimiento, graduate profile, final paragraph, fetched 2026-08-16

stops.name: Centro Cultural Haroldo Conti, Yéssica de Adrogué
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio only
stops.campa: She dances in Yéssica de Adrogué, directed by Rodrigo Arena, at the Centro Cultural Haroldo Conti, which stands on the old naval school grounds on Avenida del Libertador. Her portfolio supplies the credit and the year and nothing else, not how she came to the company. It is the beginning of the longest working relationship the record holds. Arena will direct her in four productions across five years, and the booking furthest forward in her calendar is still one of his.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.8
suggested_refs: Centro Cultural Haroldo Conti, Av. del Libertador 8151, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Edificio de La Prensa, the case against contemporary dance
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio and independently listed as a 2022 festival credit on her UNA graduate page
stops.campa: In the Edificio de La Prensa on Avenida de Mayo, the palace a newspaper built and the city now keeps as a house of culture, she performs in El caso Arena Rodrigo contra la danza contemporánea, directed by Rodrigo Arena, for the Festival Internacional de Buenos Aires. Evelyn Caneto photographs it. Her university's graduate page lists the 2022 festival credit on its own account, so the claim does not stand on her portfolio alone. The title names a lawsuit: Arena Rodrigo, plaintiff, against contemporary dance.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.5, photo credit Evelyn Caneto
UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile (2022 FIBA credit)
suggested_refs: Edificio de La Prensa, Casa de la Cultura, Av. de Mayo 575, Buenos Aires

stops.name: El Cultural San Martín, a season in five words
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio; no dates, run length or performance count recorded anywhere
stops.campa: The piece takes a season at El Cultural San Martín on Sarmiento, in the same year it plays the festival in the old newspaper palace on Avenida de Mayo. The portfolio records that season in five words and no dates: how many performances, to what houses, across how many weeks, is nowhere stated. The season is dated 2022 and nothing narrows it further. The theatre keeps its own record of the year, and that record is not reachable from outside the building.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.5
suggested_refs: El Cultural San Martín, Sarmiento 1551, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Uniclub, the presentation of PAJUERANA
stops.date_confidence: the portfolio dates the show 2022; Bandcamp dates the record's release to 1 October 2021, which is not a conflict, a presentation show postdating its release being ordinary
stops.campa: On Guardia Vieja, in Almagro by the Abasto, she performs in the show presenting PAJUERANA, the record by Chocolate Remix, directed by Rodrigo Arena. The address sits in Comuna 5; Abasto is the informal name for the ground around the old market rather than a barrio of its own. Bandcamp dates the release to the first of October 2021 and the portfolio dates the show to 2022. A record presentation that follows its release by months is ordinary, the more so in a city whose venues were still reopening through late 2021. Daniela Cilli photographs the night.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.13, photo credit Daniela Cilli

stops.name: Teatro Auditorium, Mar del Plata, the first city that is not hers
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio only; no festival programme was reachable
stops.campa: El caso Arena travels to the Teatro Auditorium on the Mar del Plata seafront, for the Festival Cuerpx, Arte y Género. It is the first time her name appears outside Buenos Aires. Her portfolio lists the four festival stops in one run of commas and does not say whether she danced every house or joined the tour partway. The festival is built around bodies and gender, which is the ground the piece already stands on, and the Auditorium is the largest theatre complex in the province, facing the water.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.5

stops.name: Teatro Lavardén, Rosario, the third city
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio only; coordinate corrected to the OpenStreetMap geocode of Plataforma Lavardén at Mendoza y Sarmiento, the earlier pin having sat some 820 m off
stops.campa: The third city of the tour year is Rosario. The house is the Lavardén at Mendoza and Sarmiento, a theatre of the 1920s that the province now runs as a platform for young work, and the festival is El Cruce. Her portfolio gives the theatre, the festival and the year, and stops there. Nothing on the festival's own side was reachable to confirm any of it. Was she on the bill for one night or for a run? El Cruce has left no programme anyone outside Rosario can ask.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.5

stops.name: Teatro Municipal de Bahía Blanca, the last located stop
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio only; coordinate corrected to the OpenStreetMap geocode of Alsina 425, the earlier pin having sat some 460 m off
stops.campa: The tour's last located stop is the Teatro Municipal on Alsina in Bahía Blanca, for the Festival Internacional de Artes Escénicas Bahía Teatro. A piece made in one city has now been carried to the coast, the river and the south: four houses in two years, danced by a woman whose name appears on no festival programme reachable from outside the country. The portfolio has a few months left to run before it is saved for the last time. After Bahía Blanca it prints nothing further about El caso Arena.

stops.name: Teatro Bombón, the venue string that splits in two
stops.date_confidence: ambiguous venue string, unresolved; the two-venue reading is named as likeliest and is unconfirmed, and the pin falls on the city-level anchor rather than on either candidate
stops.campa: Page three of the portfolio lists the venues of El Acuário in one run of commas: FIBA, Teatro Bombón Gesell, Centro Cultural Recoleta CABA, 2023. Read as one name, Teatro Bombón Gesell matches nothing anywhere. Read as two, with a comma dropped, it is Teatro Bombón, the roving Buenos Aires cycle that stages work in borrowed rooms, and its Villa Gesell edition. A cycle with no fixed address leaves no gazetteer entry either way. The comma is missing and no second document exists to put it back.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.3 (ambiguous venue string, unresolved)

stops.name: Centro Cultural Recoleta, El Acuário at the festival
stops.date_confidence: year attested in the portfolio and independently listed as a 2023 festival credit on her UNA graduate page
stops.campa: At the Centro Cultural Recoleta on Junín she performs in El Acuário, directed by Janaina Leite, the Brazilian artist whose theatre sets documentary and pornographic material against each other on the same stage. Leite is the only director from outside Argentina in her record, and this is the second year running that the Festival Internacional de Buenos Aires appears in it. Her university's graduate page lists the credit on its own account, which little else in her working life carries. Lau Castro photographs the production.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.3, photo credit Lau Castro Foto
UNA Artes del Movimiento graduate profile (2023 FIBA credit)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the page with the spaced letters
stops.date_confidence: attested by the PDF's own metadata, CreationDate D:20230630223732
stops.campa: The first page of the portfolio carries no sentence, only a name set with a space between every letter, E m i l i a P o r t m a n, and three words beneath it: bailarina, performer, creadora. The legal name is nowhere on that page, nor on the one after it. It is one layer down, in the file's metadata, where the author field reads Emilia Massacesi and the title field reads Emili Portman porfolio 2023, misspelled, as saved. Only one of the two names is meant to be read, and it is the one set in spaced capitals.
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.1 and file metadata (/Author, /Title, /Creator and /Producer Canva)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, fourteen pages under one byline
stops.date_confidence: attested by the PDF's own metadata; the document was never updated, which is why it records nothing after mid-2023
stops.campa: Fourteen pages, built in Canva, linked from her university's graduate page as a file on a drive: this is the whole public account of her working life. The document was made on the thirtieth of June 2023 and never revised, so the record does not thin out after 2023; the source stops, and everything later has to be got from Instagram. Page two opens with a sentence that sets six occupations in one row and ranks none of them, and the pole pages outnumber the theatre pages.
stops.quote: Soy artista escénica, performer, directora, docente, modelo y pole dancer. Vivo y trabajo en la Ciudad de Buenos Aires
sources: Massacesi portfolio PDF, p.2 and file metadata (/CreationDate D:20230630223732)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, teaching Danza Moderna and the Método Muller
stops.date_confidence: undated institutional statement, current as of the 2026 fetch; the transmission claim is one-directional, and nothing asserts she met either Muller or Limón
stops.campa: She teaches Danza Moderna and the Método Muller in schools and studios across the city and Greater Buenos Aires. The method is Jennifer Muller's, made by a dancer who was principal of the José Limón company through the 1960s and who was herself commissioned, decades later, to make a work for Buenos Aires. Limón never brought his own company south; the line reaches this city through Muller, and through the studio rooms that teach her method. What Emilia Massacesi carries into those rooms by day is the codified expressive technique she works against by night under another name.
stops.quote: Se desempeña como docente de Danza Moderna y Método Muller en diversas escuelas y estudios de la Ciudad y del Gran Buenos Aires.
stops.quote_source: UNA Departamento de Artes del Movimiento, graduate profile, fetched 2026-08-16

stops.name: Almagro, La Casa del Hoteo
stops.date_confidence: start year derived by subtraction from a 10 July 2026 post reading three years; her role at the club is unstated by every reachable source
stops.campa: In Almagro she keeps a night called La Casa del Hoteo, tagged in her own bio to a club account. Whether she owns it, teaches at it, dances in it or simply hosts it, no reachable source states. The name is a joke about hustling that the city reads at once and that no dictionary carries. Her portfolio, saved and closed in June of the same year the house begins, does not mention it at all. From the street the house amounts to a handle in a bio and one anniversary image.
sources: Instagram @em.port_ bio, fetched 2026-08-16
suggested_refs: Almagro Exotic Club, the venue behind the tagged handle, whose own account is access-restricted

stops.name: Almagro, three years of the house
stops.date_confidence: post date attested by fetch and re-fetch of the profile listing
stops.campa: On the tenth of July 2026 she posts an image whose lettering reads 3 AÑOS ALMÁGRO, with the club's own EXOTIC Club wordmark set between that line and the line LACASADELHOTEO. It is the only date attached to the house in any public source, and it fixes the beginning by subtraction: three years back from July 2026 is 2023. The club's own account, shut to anyone without a password, cannot be asked to confirm it. The stylised type carries an accent the barrio does not have.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, flags in her heart, and a costume in dispute
stops.date_confidence: date, caption, tags and like count confirmed by direct fetch and independently by shortcode decode to 2026-01-15 19:36:57 UTC; the costume identification is contradicted between passes and is left open here
stops.campa: On the fifteenth of January 2026 she posts images captioned Banderas en mi corazón, tagging the Temptation Show and the photographer Romina Soledad. The post takes 107 likes and one comment, which an unauthenticated reader cannot see. What she is wearing is disputed and stays disputed: one pass called the number Fidel Castro, cigar included, and a later viewing of the images in the application called the olive beret with the red star Che Guevara's, specifically. Neither reading can be recovered by fetch, and the post names no venue and no city. Whose flags, then, and whose beret?

stops.name: Buenos Aires, two accounts and one pseudonym
stops.date_confidence: follower counts and account states attested by fetch at this date
stops.campa: Two accounts carry the stage name. The public one, @em.port_, verified, holds 5,191 followers. The private one, @emili.portman, holds 2,102 and admits no one uninvited. Her university's graduate page links both, which is an unusual thing for an institution to do with a locked account. The bio of the open one runs four short lines: a name in spaced capitals, a house in Almagro, and two dates in August, one of them six days off and the other twelve.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Illusion Lov€
stops.date_confidence: announced and unperformed; no venue, city, hour or tagged account appears in any reachable source
stops.campa: The second line of her bio reads 28/8 Illusion Lov€, the last letter written as a currency sign. There is no venue, no city, no hour, no tagged account, nothing at all to follow, and no other account reachable from outside carries the name. It is the furthest forward entry in the record and the least documented of them: a date, a name, and a symbol standing in for a letter. Six days after the cabaret in Barracas, something called Illusion Lov€ is supposed to happen.
